title: Specific differences in form are mainly differences of relative magnitude

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Specific differences in form are mainly differences of relative magnitude

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The essential differences in form between species of the same group are differences of proportion or relative magnitude (Aristotle's 'excess and defect'), and these are the main cause of specific differences.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is precisely this difference of relative magnitudes, this Aristotelian “excess and defect” in the case of form, which our co-ordinate method is especially adapted to analyse, and to reveal and demonstrate as the main cause of what (again in the Aristotelian sense) we term “specific” differences.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Specific differences as excess and defect”. Scope: species within the same zoological class or genus

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Morphometric decomposition is feasible with extensive public data, but substantial interpretation is needed to define essential difference and causation. Results would resolve selected clades rather than the full zoological generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Decompose interspecific shape differences within clades into size/proportion changes versus topological, meristic and novel-structure changes, then estimate the fraction of diagnostic variation explained by relative magnitudes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
“Essential” and “main cause” lack thresholds.

Species diagnoses and causal differences are not identical.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Relative magnitude versus discrete novelty can be scored with existing scans and matrices for some groups. 'Main cause of specific differences' still needs a threshold and a choice of characters, and both choices move the result. The data can show that proportions dominate in particular clades and cannot underwrite the general causal wording.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within genera or classes, partition species differences into relative magnitudes (uniform scaling, shear and simple gradients) versus discrete, localized novelties. The claim is supported if most between-species shape distance lies in the proportional part; a large share of discrete character changes would refute 'mainly'.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Well-sampled clades are a minority of classes and genera.

What counts as the main cause depends on whether landmarks or presence-absence characters are given priority.
